This first bail application under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 438 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant- Rahul Rami S/o Purushottam Rami for grant of anticipatory bail, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.71/2025 registered at Police Station Madhav Nagar, District Ujjain (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 376(2), 506 of IPC.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.

Earlier complainant had lodged FIR on 24.09.2024 vide crime no.506/2024 against the applicant under Section 420 of IPC where in the complainant never mentioned that she has been raped by the applicant on 13.03.2023 to 11.09.2023 and in that case the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9650 2 MCRC-12939-2025 applicant has been granted bail.
He further submitted that in the present case, FIR has been lodged on 11.02.2025 near about 2 years after the alleged first date of incident, therefore, it is clear case of false implication.
Sufficient evidence is not available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
There is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with evidence.
He will cooperate with the investigation.
On these contentions, on the ground of parity, learned counsel prays for allowing the application for grant of anticipatory bail.

3. Learned counsel for the Objector opposed the prayer on the ground that earlier on 19.11.2023 complainant has given written complaint to the Superintendent of Police, district Ujjain wherein she has narrated the incident but there is not delay in lodging the FIR.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and prays for dismissal of the anticipatory bail application, but fairly admits that in the earlier complaint there is no mention of rape rather there is mention of threatening to commit rape.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the fact that in the earlier complaint registered as FIR No.506/2024, there is no mention of rape committed upon the complainant on 13.03.2023 to 11.09.2023, looking to the FIR in the instant case which is lodged on 11.02.2025 by inordinate delay,
raises a ground that there was enmity between the parties, this Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9650 3 MCRC-12939-2025 is inclined to grant benefit of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

8. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump and / or breach of any of the conditions of bail, this order will come to an end and applicant will be liable to be arrested by the concerned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9650 4 MCRC-12939-2025 authorities.
9. The trial Court shall get these conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
